title: De Vries Sensible Storage State Law

invariants.evidence: Adds one generic sensible-storage primitive to the single SWAP5 kernel/process architecture; no use-case-specific SWAP variant is introduced.
Production code contains no files, paths, parsing, format or unit-number dependencies.

Mixture heat-capacity properties are explicit immutable configuration by intended use and calculated storage quantities are results; no forcing, numerical policy or committed state is mixed into the parameter object.
No persistent per-column dynamic or restart state is added.
No Newton, Jacobian or other heavy solver scratch is introduced.
The scalar law is layout-agnostic and suitable for batched implementation, but SoA/SIMD/cache behavior is not benchmarked here.
The algebra mutates no committed state and can be trial-local, but transaction-aware publication into an accepted energy ledger is deferred.
The state law is deterministic and cheaply recomputable from explicit endpoint data, with no hidden history.
The formulation is over arbitrary endpoint states and contains no day, month, year, midnight or fixed timestep assumption.
No coupling-window duration or calendar boundary is encoded.
The state law is conservation/coupling-ready accounting infrastructure, but coupling runtime composition is outside EB-I05.
No groundwater head/flux interface behavior is changed.
Water state and fluxes are only consumed as inputs; EB-I05 cannot alter, repair or relax the water balance.
No groundwater response sensitivity/tangent is changed or added.
Evaluation requires no additional full SWAP solve or predictor/corrector execution.
No heavy per-column solver object or persistent storage is introduced, but hundred-thousand-column throughput is not qualified.
The primitive is column/control-volume local; tile fractions and MODFLOW-cell aggregation remain external runtime/coupler concerns.
No deep-vadose component behavior is changed.
No deep-vadose/direct-groundwater transition behavior is changed.
The linear-mixture storage law is independent of a specific Richards solver and consumes only water content and thermal parameters.
The current SWAP heat-capacity physics is represented without importing legacy globals; source-bound constants are test inputs rather than duplicated production constants.
No HeadCalc or soil-water-solver internal arrays are referenced.
Physical mixture properties are explicit and no numerical policy changes them; latent/vapor/phase physics is explicitly outside scope rather than silently approximated.
The primitive is constant-cost scalar algebra, but bounded-cost behavior within complete difficult-column runtime composition is not measured here.
The admitted restricted/reference thermal implementation remains byte-identical and available; EB-I05 does not replace it.
The result exposes exact, temperature and composition components plus a decomposition residual; runtime-wide diagnostics/publication are deferred.
Unused columns incur no added persistent state or workspace cost from EB-I05.
System composition, ledger publication, boundary transport and tile/coupler aggregation remain outside this local storage primitive.
No .swp, filesystem, midnight, one-day or mandatory-MODFLOW dependency is present.
EB-I05 is explicitly assessed against all 30 SWAP core architecture invariants in this audit.

hard_nonclaims: No full SWAP5 energy balance is qualified.
No latent heat, freeze/thaw enthalpy or vapor transport is represented.
No temperature-dependent thermophysical-property law is qualified.
No pressure, chemical or salinity enthalpy is represented.
The exact affine-state claim is restricted to 0 <= theta <= theta_sat and does not cover the admitted solver's tiny over-saturation tolerance/clipping region.
EB-I05 does not replace or modify the admitted soil-temperature solver.
A future governing-equation change that includes composition storage is not claimed to preserve the current temperature trajectory without separate qualification.
No liquid advective-energy transport or donor-temperature rule is qualified.
Runtime commit/rollback publication, MultiSWAP throughput and bounded-cost behavior are not qualified.
Independent verification and canonical admission are not claimed.
